target_customer: Enterprises, banks, contact centers and governments needing deepfake and synthetic media detection
problem: Deepfakes and AI generated media enable fraud and disinformation, and organizations cannot tell real from fake audio, video and images.
business_model: Enterprise usage based API, SDK and platform subscriptions (RealAPI, RealScan, RealCall, RealMeeting)

founders.name: Ben Colman
founders.background_notes: Former Goldman Sachs VP per TechCrunch Oct 2023. Company began as a nonprofit research project ahead of the 2020 election per a search summary of interviews.

founders.name: Ali Shahriyari
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by TechCrunch and DCVC; not listed on the YC page.

founders.name: Gaurav Bharaj
founders.background_notes: Led R&D at the AI Foundation per TechCrunch; named as co-founder by TechCrunch and DCVC.

investors: Partnership Fund for New York City

competitors.name: Truepic
competitors.what: Photo and video authentication and provenance rather than detection
competitors.funding_then: $26M Series B led by M12 in Sept 2021

competitors.name: Sensity (formerly Deeptrace)
competitors.what: Deepfake detection for law enforcement, KYC vendors and forensics

technical_complexity.rationale: Detecting synthetic audio, video and images needs ML research that must keep pace with new generators; founders came from the AI Foundation R&D team per TechCrunch.

defensibility.rationale: Detection models trained on many generators and enterprise integrations are hard to copy quickly, but accuracy claims are contested across vendors and the arms race favours generators.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch (2023) names Microsoft as an incumbent with detection tools; no acquisition of Reality Defender found, and KPMG took an undisclosed minority stake (reported 2026).

market_need_then: Deepfakes were a growing concern around the 2020 US election, and the company began as a nonprofit research project on that threat; Truepic's $26M raise in Sept 2021 shows investor interest.

branding.name_origin: CEO said on a podcast that as the name suggests, we defend reality; no further origin found.
branding.domain_note: Uses realitydefender.com, exact match domain; acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission driven security language, market leader claims

branding.community_and_virality: Awards: RSA Conference Innovation Sandbox most innovative startup (2025 per company site), SXSW 2023 and Gartner recognition per company materials

brand_strength.rationale: The name states the mission and has won security industry awards and press, but sources show no consumer or viral brand effect.

outcome_analysis: Reality Defender began as a research project, joined YC W22, then raised a $15M Series A led by DCVC in October 2023, expanded to $33M in October 2024 and later took an undisclosed KPMG stake. The generative AI boom after 2022 created a large timing tailwind for enterprise deepfake detection, and awards and bank case studies suggest an enterprise sales engine. Its main risk is the detection arms race.
notes: The October 2024 extension brought the Series A total to $33M; the extension amount is not stated in sources opened, so it is null. Aggregators disagree on the lead (Illuminate Financial per press release; ZoomInfo says Booz Allen; Seedtable says YC) and StartupIntros gives $48M total raised. Earlier YC or seed funding was not found. KPMG minority stake with undisclosed terms was reported by Biometric Update (Sept 2026 URL) and not recorded as a round. TechCrunch 2023 names Sentinel and DeepMedia as rivals, but they are not shown to exist at founding.
